summary: An ext2 volume stopped under writes, judged by Rach2's next writable mount and its check first, then the host's e2fsck -fn and the sentinel files, against the same volume powered off in order; the program is tests/cases/machine/ext2stop_scenario.c

cases.behavior: An ext2 volume that QEMU's quit stops under two writers and a loop of syncs, with sentinel files synced and four removed files held open, mounts writable at the next boot with its check keeping only lost blocks and orphan inodes for e2fsck, the held inodes and any file a writer removed whose free the stop kept from the disk, keeps its sentinels and takes a write; e2fsck -fn finds in it, before and after that mount, only those inodes, as many as the check counted, their bits and blocks and the free counts; and the same volume powered off as a user stops the machine, the control, is clean and needs no check

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machines and removes the three disks, the stopped volume's copy among them, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: write the control disk's MBR with mkmbr and make its 64 MiB ext2 volume with mke2fs, with the installed root's features, a fixed identifier and hash seed

boot os-real from its RAM image, log in as root, mount the volume, write and sync the sentinels, hold four files open, remove them and sync, start the writers and the syncs, power off with them running and end the machine
make the stop disk's volume as the control's, boot, run the same workload and end the machine with QMP's quit once both writers are at their hundredth file
copy the stopped disk whole into the disk stopped, before any boot mounts it
boot with the stopped disk and the control, mount each in turn, compare its sentinels, write a file, unmount it, and power off
run e2fsck -fn on the stopped copy, on the stopped volume after Rach2's mount and on the control, in the image helper machine

assertions.checks: mkmbr writes the control disk's table and mke2fs makes its volume, each exiting 0
/proc/mounts has /dev/disk0p1 /mnt/s ext2 rw 0 0, a mount that writes back, which the scenario prints
the eight sentinels are written and synced
four files are made, opened by the shell, printed as HELD=N with inode numbers above 10, removed and synced
both writers print that they reached their hundredth file
poweroff, with the writers running and the held files open, says shutdown: /dev/disk0p1: unmounted before the kernel's goodbye
the poweroff left the control's superblock state 1, unmounted cleanly
mkmbr and mke2fs make the stop disk's volume, each exiting 0
the stop boot mounts its volume rw, as the control
the sentinels are written and synced
the four held files are made, numbered, removed and synced
both writers reach their hundredth file, and QMP's quit ends the machine under them
the stop left the superblock state 0, the valid bit clear
the next boot mounts the stopped volume as /dev/disk0p1 /mnt/s ext2 rw 0 0

the kernel's check of it says ext2: check: L lost blocks, M orphan inodes, kept for e2fsck, with M at least 4: the held inodes, whose blocks count among the lost, and the files a writer removed whose free the stop kept from the disk after their entries, and no fault
each sentinel is byte for byte what wrote it
a file is written there and synced
the volume unmounts
the control mounts as /dev/disk1p1 /mnt/s ext2 rw 0 0
the kernel does not check the control, which its poweroff left clean
each of the control's sentinels is what wrote it
a file is written on the control and synced
the control unmounts

e2fsck -fn on the copy taken before any mount exits 0, or 4 with nothing but its passes, a removed inode's zero deletion time, an unattached inode that is not a held one, block bitmap differences that are each a block marked used that nothing names, inode bitmap differences that are each an inode marked used that nothing uses, the free counts, its answers of no and its summary, and with as many unattached and freed inodes as the kernel's check counted orphans
e2fsck -fn on the stopped volume after Rach2's mount, write and unmount finds the same and nothing else
e2fsck -fn on the control after both boots exits 0

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case stops a machine under writes to a disk of its own and checks the disk on the host after, which the installed machine's disk cannot be
